        # We need g(n+2) and g(n+3) to calculate g(n+4)
        
        # The relation is: g(n) + g(n+1) = g(n+2)g(n+3) - 840
        # Let m = n+2. We are solving for g(m+1).
        # g(m-2) + g(m-1) = g(m)g(m+1) - 840
        # g(m)g(m+1) = g(m-2) + g(m-1) + 840
        
        g_m_2 = sequence[n-2]
        g_m_1 = sequence[n-1]
        g_m = sequence[n] # This is g(n+2)
        
        numerator = g_m_2 + g_m_1 + 840
        denominator = g_m
        
        if numerator % denominator != 0:
            return None # Not an integer
        
        return numerator // denominator

    # Start from n=2 (calculating g(5))

        g_m_1 = g_current[m-2]
        g_m = g_current[m-1]

        numerator = g_m_2 + g_m_1 + 840
        denominator = g_m
